claims.text: Superconductivity in HEAs outside Nb-Ta and well-ordered titanium-heavy-transition-metal systems is governed primarily by local chemical short-range order.
Local chemical short-range order modulates electron-phonon coupling strength.
Increasing short-range order strengthens electron-phonon coupling and raises Tc.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the proposed titanium-rich, heavy-transition-metal alloy as a disordered solid solution.
The proposed as-cast alloy has only weak or mixed short-range order.
Annealing below the order-disorder transition can promote local chemical short-range order without causing long-range phase separation.
An annealing temperature around 0.8 times the melting temperature is suitable for promoting short-range order while retaining a single phase.
Annealing-induced atomic redistribution produces local chemical short-range order.
Short-range order creates more uniform local atomic environments favorable for electron-phonon interactions.
Enhanced short-range order reduces randomness in local potential landscapes.
Reduced local-potential randomness minimizes disorder-induced electron scattering.
Local chemical ordering refines the phonon spectrum.
Local chemical ordering increases the effective electron-phonon coupling constant lambda.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling enhances superconducting pairing and increases Tc.
Enhanced short-range order may sharpen the superconducting transition.
The annealed alloy will have a higher Tc than the as-cast alloy.
The annealed alloy will have a narrower superconducting transition than the as-cast alloy.
Pair-distribution-function analysis or high-resolution TEM will detect increased short-range-order signatures after annealing.
The random atomic configuration of the as-cast alloy causes stronger electron scattering, lower Tc, and a broader superconducting transition.
Phase separation or crystallization would take the material outside the intended single-phase high-entropy regime.
